column4: Establishment of Agricultural Bioprocessing, Imaging, and Sensing Laboratory
column6: Construction of an Integrated Engineering Building
column8:
The agriculture and fishery sector is vital in the country’s efforts to recover from the effects of the CoVid19 pandemic. At present, the low productivity of the local agricultural producers in the Caraga region is magnified by the disruptions in the food chain and decreased economic activity during the community quarantine period. The CoVid19 pandemic exposed the vulnerabilities of the sector and highlighted the need to improve regional food security. As the region’s premier state university, CSU positions itself as a lead agency for research and development for agriculture. CSU already has a pool of technical experts specializing in agricultural processing and food engineering who may be tapped to conduct research in addressing the food security agenda of the government. With the challenges brought by the COVID-19 pandemic, more efforts are required to ensure availability, accessibility, and affordability of safe and nutritious food. However, the Caraga region has no existing laboratory for agricultural bioprocessing that could improve the nutritional content and longer the shelf life of the local products. The proposed bioprocessing, imaging and sensing laboratory is very timely in the new normal situation to support the efforts of the government to ensure food security. This bioprocessing laboratory will be in-housed at the new CEIT Complex of the University with 15 m x 15 m floor area.

The bioprocessing, imaging and sensing laboratory primarily aims to position itself as the premier and renowned agricultural engineering laboratory that will in-house the development of new and innovative food products from locally-available agricultural commodities; spearhead the conduct of non-destructive quality assessment protocols for agricultural commodities through imaging and near-infrared spectroscopy techniques; aid in the development of advanced technologies to reduce postharvest losses, improve shelf-life, and maintain product quality of perishables; lead in the conduct of basic researches on the physicochemical, thermal and sensory properties of agricultural products; provide technical assistance to farmers and local food process industries; and provide facility for students and faculty instruction, research, and extension.

column4: Sustainability of Neritic Tuna Fisheries in Southern Philippines
column6: Completion of Center for Biodiversity Studies in SOCSKSARGEN
column8:
Neritic tuna species are crucial to the economy, ecology, and food security of Southern Philippines, especially in Sarangani Bay, where they support both small-scale and commercial fishers. However, recent assessments show that these tuna stocks are increasingly threatened by overfishing, juvenile catch, bycatch, and weak monitoring systems. Climate change further intensifies these risks by altering ocean conditions, affecting tuna spawning, migration, and food availability.

To address these challenges, the project aims to develop a science-based, policy-oriented, and community-driven framework for sustaining neritic tuna fisheries. It will integrate ecological and socioeconomic research, fisheries monitoring, and stakeholder participation. In partnership with BFAR, local governments, fisherfolk groups, and commercial operators, the project will gather real-time data, review fishing practices, and recommend management measures such as seasonal closures, gear regulations, and stock recovery strategies. Awareness and capacity-building initiatives will also help engage communities as co-managers of marine resources.

Ultimately, the project seeks to secure a resilient, sustainable, and equitable tuna industry in Southern Mindanao, aligned with national development goals, fisheries regulations, and global commitments to marine conservation.

column4: Strengthening MIRDC’s Metalworking Facility to Support the Philippine’s Self Reliance Defense Program (SRDP)

MIRDC has developed specialized facilities, including the Die and Mold Solution Center, Gear Making Facility, Heat Treatment, Welding and Fabrication, Metal Casting, and the Advanced Manufacturing Center, to support various industries. While these facilities could address the Armed Forces of the Philippines' (AFP) metalworking needs, restrictions on producing ammunition and military armaments limit their direct defense applications.

Republic Act 12024, the Self-Reliant Defense Posture Revitalization Act (SRDP), underscores the Philippine government’s aim to strengthen its defense industry and reduce reliance on imports. The act mandates the Department of Science and Technology (DOST) as a key partner to advance research, innovation, and local manufacturing.

A proposal to upgrade MIRDC’s metalworking facility aligns with SRDP goals, focusing on modernizing infrastructure, integrating advanced equipment, and enhancing workforce skills. Notably, the plan includes a forging facility critical for producing defense components like armor plates, rifle barrels, and wing spars. This will support the Office of Defense Technology Research and Industry Development (ODTRID) in developing high-quality prototypes.

Beyond defense, the facility can serve other industries, such as railways, by producing essential components locally. This initiative aims to boost production efficiency, reduce import dependency, and foster long-term industrial growth across sectors.

column4: Enhancement of Analysis and Testing Services in Support of the SRDP
column6: SRDP Support Program
column7: Metals Industry Research and Development Center
column8:
Almost all parts and components of a product includes metals and metal alloys. Steel is one of the common materials used in the manufacture of products. At present, steel is still the best choice in the manufacture of products because of its affordability and environment friendly since it can be recycled to produce another product. 

Republic Act No. 12024, “AN ACT REVITALIZING AND STRENGTHENING THE SELF-RELIANT DEFENSE POSTURE PROGRAM AND PROMOTING THE DEVELOPMENT OF A NATIONAL DEFENSE INDUSTRY PURSUANT THERETO AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR” was signed into law last October 8, 2024. The said Act aims to develop related metals and allied engineering industries in the Philippines for self-sufficiency in terms of producing weaponry and equipment for its armed forces.

The Metals Industry Research and Development Center (MIRDC) of the Department of Science and Technology (DOST) specialized in metal and metal products. Most of the defense weaponry are largely made of metals. Among the strategic defense industries where MIRDC can actively take part of is in the shipbuilding, aircraft and space industries.

Provisions of necessary tests and calibration facilities for the said industries are the focus of this project. Weld quality is one of the main concerns in shipbuilding. Reliability of weld joints shall be maintained and shall be monitored using different tests/inspection techniques. The same is true with the manufacture of aircraft. All parts and components shall work properly. Nondestructive inspection after the manufacture of these parts and components ensure their effectiveness. 

The Self-Reliant Defense Posture (SRDP) program of the government needs support in terms of appropriate tests and calibration services that will ensure reliable parts and components. At present, some of these common tests and calibration equipment have existed at MIRDC but specialized test facilities are still unavailable. These specialized tests will validate the effectiveness of the adjustment in the design during the R&D activities and will also support the local manufacturing industries achieve reliable parts and components.



Need
Testing Facility to support the SRDP is essential to the achievement of its goal. Technical support, particularly the availability of material and performance test facility is needed to validate the effectiveness of the R&D activities conducted through SRDP program. 


Solution
Establishment of test and calibration facilities that support SRDP’s R&D activities. This will help researchers validate their design for the proper performance of the product they are developing. The primary function of the said facility will guide the researchers on the appropriate adjustment in the development of their products.

Differentiation
This project will result to the availability of necessary test and calibration facility to support SRDP’s R&D activities. This will enhance our self sufficiency with regards to National Security. It will also improve our local manufacturers for the provision of quality control test and calibration facility during pre-acceptance of delivered materials, during production line, and batch testing of their produced products.

column4: Coatings and Surface Engineering (CaSE) facility enhancement in Support to the SRDP Program and other applications
column6: Surface Engineering R&D Program
column7: Metals Industry Research and Development Center
column8:
Surface engineering is essential to improving the functionality and performance of metallic materials. Advances in the field include the application of protective coatings for better mechanical and tribological properties, surface modifications for corrosion protection, and bioactive treatments for medical implants. Surface engineering techniques are actively being used in the metals and engineering industries to improve corrosion protection, wear resistance, and component enhancement. These developments underscore the interdisciplinary nature of surface engineering, which combines chemistry, physics, and materials science to promote innovation and tackle emerging challenges in various sectors.

The surface engineering facility of the DOST-MIRDC serves multiple critical functions that contribute to the agency’s mission, the broader community, and the economy. The MPRD may provide the infrastructure necessary for pioneering research in the field of surface engineering, particularly in functional coatings, leading to new discoveries and innovations in the field. It is understood that a well-equipped facility can accommodate a variety of research projects across different scientific and engineering disciplines. Currently, the surface engineering facility of DOST-MIRDC accommodates coating applications via electroplating and anodizing processes only. Moreover, the Center offers coating characterization and test such as mechanical testing, surface roughness, microstructural, and chemical composition analysis. 

One research area that the Center envisions to provide support is the defense sector. With the recent signing of the REPUBLIC ACT NO. 12024 or known as the “Self-Reliant Defense Posture (SRDP) Revitalization Act” on October 8, 2024, this opened doors for future research collaborations on human security and national defense. R&D initiatives have already been undertaken by the Center when it developed the BUHAWI or “Building a Universal Mount for Heavy-Barrel Automated Weapon Integration” in partnership with Philippine Navy’s Naval Research and Technology Development Center (NRTDC) and Mechatronics and Robotics Society of the Philippines (MRSP), and the Project COBRA - “Controller Operated Battle Ready Armament” with Philippine Army (PH Army) and the Mechatronics and Robotics Society of the Philippines (MRSP) as R&D partners. The coating and surface engineering requirements, however, of these technologies have not been explored yet considering its exposure to harsh environment and extreme conditions which may later affect their performance, protection capability and durability. The MIRDC has demonstrated its capability on building military equipment, but still lacks on the area of coatings and surface engineering. It is worthy to note that metal, particularly steel, is still the primary material used in many military vehicles and equipment.
Enhancing the surface engineering facility of MIRDC with various coating and surface engineering equipment, characterization and electrochemical measurement techniques, is a strategic investment that will support the needs of the SRDP in terms of coatings and surface engineering. In 2023, Balik Scientist Dr. Eugene B. Caldona helped the MIRDC fine-tune its Surface Engineering R&D roadmap. One research sub-area in this roadmap is on the coatings for high performance applications such as the protective equipment in the defense industry, among other functional coating applications. He also welcomed the idea of having a R&D collaboration with the Center and even offered his laboratory in the Department of Coatings and Polymeric Materials at North Dakota State University (NDSU) for our local researchers to be exposed to advanced coating techniques through technology benchmarking and short-term trainings.

Below is an initial list of possible research projects under the CaSE:
Projects Supporting the SRDP Program
A.1: Optimization of the Reduced Concentration of Blackening Treatment Solution for Magnetite Surface Coating Process
A.2: Microstructural Functionally Graded Armor Plates
A.3: Atmospheric Plasma Sprayed Coatings for Military Equipment Applications
B. Other Applications
B.1: Metal Corrosion Protection Using Epoxy/Polyaniline Coating Embedded with Rice Husk-Derived Silica
B.2: Corrosion Inhibition Properties of Water Hyacinth-Mediated Silver and Gold Nanoparticles on Selected Metals
B.3: Development of Protective Coatings for Metallic Heritage Conservation

By equipping the researchers with the necessary tools and environment to conduct high-quality research, MIRDC can foster groundbreaking discoveries and stimulate economic growth through technological advancements and industry collaborations.

column4: Metagenome of Chicken Intestinal Microbiome  under Antibiotic-Free and Conventional Broiler  Production Systems
column6: Completion of Center for Biodiversity Studies in SOCSKSARGEN
column8:
The proposed study will be carried to determine the chicken intestinal microbiome under antibiotic-free and conventional broiler production systems using metagenomic analysis.

Experimental Design and Treatments  The study will be conducted in a Completely Randomized Design with two treatments replicated 10 times. Each experimental unit (a cage) will have at least 
two sample animals. The sample animals will be subjected to the following treatments:  

T1: Antibiotic-Free Broiler Production System. For this treatment, the sample animals will not receive any antibiotic, instead, an alternative strategy will be employed in their production.  

T2: Conventional Broiler Production System. For this treatment, the sample animals will receive antibiotic based on the conventional practices in broiler production.

Experimental Layout and Randomization  

The experiment will be set-up inside the poultry house. Twenty chicken cages will be prepared in which at least two sample animals will be randomly assigned and subjected to any of the two treatments 

Preparation and Rearing of Sample Animals  

Day-old chicks of uniform sizes and vigor will be purchased from the market. At least two chicks will be assigned to each cage. The animals will be reared according to the established broiler production system except for the administration of antibiotics which will depend on the assigned treatment for each chick.  

Administration of Antibiotics  
Only the sample animals assigned to T2 will receive the usual dosage of antibiotics based on the conventional broiler production system. The remaining samples will receive alternative care based on the veterinarian’s recommendation.  

Collection of Intestinal Samples  
Sample animals will be harvested and processed when 80% of all samples reach the marketable size and quality, usually within one month of production. Intestines will be collected, and contents will be removed for metagenomics analysis.  

Metagenomic Analysis  
Intestinal contents will be sent out for next-generation sequencing (NGS). NGS sequences will be subjected to statistics and bioinformatics

column4: Microbial and Physico-Chemical Water Quality Monitoring of the Commercial and Vendo Machines in General Santos City: Basis for Policy Action and  Recommendation in the Local Government Unit
column6: Completion of Center for Biodiversity Studies in SOCSKSARGEN
column8:
In the implementation process, the following will be considered:  

Sampling Sites: Sampling sites will be selected to represent various locations across General Santos City, including market water suppliers and vendo machine locations. Sites will be chosen based on population density, geographic distribution, and accessibility.  

Protocol: Water samples will be collected from selected sites using sterile sampling bottles according to standardized procedures. Samples will be collected at regular intervals, including peak and off-peak hours, to capture variations in water quality.  

Parameters for Analysis: Water samples will be analyzed for a comprehensive range of parameters, including but not limited to microbial contaminants (e.g., Total coliform bacteria, Total Fecal Count, Total Heterotrophic Count), and physical parameters (e.g., pH, TDS, and Hardness) following Philippines National Standard for Drinking Water (2007) 
 
Laboratory Analysis: Collected water samples will be transported to MSU Microbiology Laboratory for analysis using appropriate methods and equipment. The analysis will be conducted by standard protocols and quality assurance measures to ensure the accuracy and reliability of results.  

Data Management and Analysis: Monitoring data will be compiled, organized, and analyzed using statistical and spatial analysis techniques. Trends and patterns in water quality will be identified, and areas of concern will be highlighted for further investigation.  

Stakeholder Engagement: Regular communication and collaboration with relevant stakeholders, including local authorities, water suppliers, and consumer groups, will be maintained throughout the project. Stakeholders will be engaged in data interpretation, decision-making, and implementation of corrective actions and preventive measures.  

Reporting and Dissemination: Findings from the monitoring project will be documented in comprehensive reports, including summaries of monitoring results, analysis of findings, and recommendations for action. Reports will be disseminated to relevant stakeholders and made accessible to the public through various channels, including online platforms and community outreach activities.  

By closely monitoring the quality of drinking water supplied by market water suppliers and vendo machines in General Santos City, this project aims to promote public health, enforce regulatory compliance, and empower consumers to make informed choices about their water consumption. Through systematic monitoring, analysis, and stakeholder engagement, the project seeks to contribute to the provision of safe and reliable drinking water for all residents of General Santos City.

column4: Development of a Knowledge Management System (KMS) for CDObites
column7: University of Science and Technology of Southern Philippines
column8:
The Development of a Knowledge Management System (KMS) for CDObites addresses a persistent challenge in startup incubation: the reliance on fragmented spreadsheets and manual tracking tools. Currently, critical data on founders, mentors, and program progress is scattered across multiple files, creating risks of errors, low transparency, and inefficiencies in mentorship matching. These gaps weaken program delivery, limit ecosystem visibility, and hinder investor confidence.
The proposed solution is a cloud-based KMS designed specifically for startup incubation. It will feature role-based dashboards that provide tailored access for founders, mentors, staff, and investors, ensuring secure and efficient information flow. A key innovation is the integration of AI-driven mentor-startup matching, which optimizes guidance by aligning founders’ needs with mentor expertise. Additionally, the system will host investment readiness kits, equipping startups with structured resources to prepare for funding opportunities and scale their ventures.
Primary beneficiaries include startup founders, mentors, incubator staff, and investors, who will gain from streamlined operations, enhanced transparency, and more effective mentorship. At a broader level, the innovation ecosystem will benefit from improved collaboration, data-driven decision-making, and higher startup success rates. Visuals such as process flow diagrams and sample dashboards will illustrate the system’s design and functionality.

column8:
The Tech4ED-DTC Project is a national digital inclusion initiative that establishes self-sustaining Centers to serve as entry points for capacity development initiatives in the countryside. The DTCs will serve as the physical landing points where capacity development initiatives are conducted in the region's provinces. By establishing DTC as close to the people of every province in the region as possible, the project involves the local government units in each province to identify digital workforce needs aligned with their respective development thrusts. The DTC shall serve as a center of capacity development on digital and information communication technology (ICT) skills based on regional and provincial development priorities and needs.
In the medium-term, the project will focus on developing a strong foundation of local talent intended to create a fertile ground for the emergence of a more robust ICT ecosystem at the regional and local levels, bringing support systems for digital workers as close to them as possible.
The project shall include construction of 2-storey DTC buildings, site development, 100 units of ICT
equipment, furniture and fixtures for each of the five Digital Skills Training Campuses in Province of
Dinagat Islands, which will serve as hubs of digital upskilling for the province's workforce.

The Tech4ED Digital Transformation Centers (DTC) Project is a national digital inclusion initiative that establishes self-sustaining Centers to serve as entry points for capacity development initiatives in the countryside. By 2028, the project aims to: 

1. Establish DTCs in:
a. 100% of regions with Level 4 DTCs;

The Smart Bulacan Province project is a collaborative initiative of the Development Academy of the Philippines, the Department of Science and Technology, and Bulacan State University to establish a data driven and technology enabled governance framework for the Province of Bulacan. The program will develop digital solutions, policy studies, and capacity building activities that support evidence-based decision making, sustainable urban and rural development, and improved delivery of public services. Through the application of smart technologies and STI governance, the project will enhance local government efficiency, promote transparency and accountability, and provide a model for smart province development in Central Luzon.

The involves the wholistic assessment of the smart province readiness of the whole province, identify inter-municipality and intra-municipality gaps, and craft a STI Plan and Provincial Smart City roadmap to provide solutions to the identified smart province gaps.
